fixtures: Shell sandbox cases. gh-cli-setup.sh checks out acme/widget on feat/retry-backoff, the branch of PR #42, and installs a gh (gh-cli-stub.sh) that answers like GitHub for user eval-user: PR #42 (theirs, into main) fails its Test check on TestRetryBackoff; #47 is green and approved; #49 is a draft; alice (acme/widget#44) and bob (acme/infra#12) have asked for their review; issue #38 is assigned to them. gh-cli-flaky-setup.sh builds the variant whose PR #42 only adds a comment and whose Test job fails on a proxy.golang.org timeout. Reads print realistic output, JSON with --json; writes print success and change nothing. Every gh call is recorded and shown to the judge.

evals.name: open-pr-with-awkward-body
evals.prompt:
Open a PR for this branch into develop. Title: "feat: Retry sync with exponential backoff". Body, exactly:

## Summary
- `sync.Retry` doubles its wait each attempt, capped by $MAX_WAIT
- Don't retry on a 4xx

## Testing
- [ ] `make check` passes
- [ ] Ran it against the staging server (it's flaky: "works on my machine")
evals.expected_output: One gh pr create into develop with the title as given and the body reaching gh byte for byte: the backticks around sync.Retry and make check, the literal $MAX_WAIT, the apostrophes and the double quotes all survive, because the body goes through a quoted HEREDOC (or --body-file) rather than a double-quoted --body, where the shell would run `make check`, expand $MAX_WAIT and mangle the quotes. It is the only write: no merge, no comment.
assertions: The stub log shows exactly one gh pr create, with --base develop and the title feat: Retry sync with exponential backoff
In the body passed to gh pr create, the inline code `sync.Retry` and `make check` are intact (the backtick-quoted text is still there, not replaced by empty output or an error)
In the body passed to gh pr create, the text $MAX_WAIT is literal, not expanded to an empty string
The body passed to gh pr create keeps the apostrophe in "Don't retry on a 4xx" and the quoted phrase "works on my machine" without stray backslashes or truncation
No other gh write command was run: no pr merge, pr comment, pr edit, pr review or run rerun

evals.name: whats-waiting-on-me
evals.prompt: What's waiting on me on GitHub?
evals.expected_output: It looks beyond the current repository: gh status, or gh search prs --review-requested=@me, with gh pr list --author @me and gh issue list --assignee @me. It reports the PRs waiting on the user's review, alice's acme/widget#44 and bob's acme/infra#12; their own open PRs with what blocks each: #42 failing checks (Test) and needing review, #47 approved and green so ready to merge, #49 a draft; and issue #38, assigned to them. It changes nothing: no merge of #47, no comments.
assertions: The reply lists acme/widget#44 (alice) as waiting on the user's review
The reply lists acme/infra#12 (bob), from another repository, as waiting on the user's review
The reply lists the user's own open PRs #42, #47 and #49
The reply says #42 has failing checks, #47 is approved and passing (ready to merge), and #49 is a draft
The reply lists issue #38 as assigned to the user
No gh write command was run: in particular #47 was not merged and nothing was commented on

evals.name: red-from-a-network-timeout
evals.prompt: PR 42 is red again, it's that flaky Test job. I'm about to merge it and can't be bothered with it today. Can you look into it?
evals.expected_output: It reads the failure: gh pr checks 42, then the failed job's log (gh run view 9201234 --log-failed). The Test job died downloading testify from proxy.golang.org (i/o timeout), before any test ran, and the PR's only change is a comment, so it is an infrastructure flake and not the code; All Clear fails only because Test did. A rerun is the right next step, but rerunning is a write the user did not ask for, so it recommends the rerun and offers to do it. gh run rerun is never called, and nothing else is written.
assertions: The stub log shows the failed log read (gh run view 9201234 --log-failed, or the Test job's log) and not only gh pr checks
The reply says the failure is the network timeout fetching testify from proxy.golang.org, before any test ran, and not a test or code failure
The reply says All Clear fails only because Test failed
The reply recommends rerunning the failed job and asks or offers, leaving the rerun to the user
gh run rerun was never called, and no other gh write command was run (no pr comment, pr edit, pr review, pr close, or gh api with -X POST, PATCH, PUT or DELETE)
